To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) MCOD is a process of change in organizations and cultures to include people from multiple social and cultural group identities and (2) MCOD has been practiced in a variety of ways and has been successful in some instances and not in others.

(1) Multicultural OD (MCOD) is the practice of building organizations and organizational culture that include people from diverse social and cultural group identities; (2) MCOD is an extension of OD that focuses on the social and cultural dimensions of organizational life; and (3) MCOD has the potential to increase organizational effectiveness, but it requires the development of a multicultural organization development competency.
MCOD can be used to build organizations and organizational cultures in which people of diverse group identities can work together effectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theory of the organization as a system and the development of methods for the study and improvement of the organization.
the ways in which people are socialized into and out of organizations, and how they are socialized into the social roles they are to play in the workplace.
the development of organizations that can accommodate multiple cultures, and the development of people who can function effectively in multicultural environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chapter describes MCOD and its practice.
MCOD is a process of organizational change designed to increase the inclusion, participation, and empowerment of multiple groups of people in an organization.

multicultural organization development (OD) is a process for building organizations that include people with multiple socially defined group identities, such as race, ethnicity, class, gender, sexual identity, religion, and others.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MCOD is the practice of building organizations and cultures that value and support the full range of human diversity.
MCOD is a process for building organizations where people of diverse backgrounds are able to contribute to the success of the organization and where they can thrive.

MCOD is a theory and practice that seeks to build and sustain organizations that are inclusive and respectful of all people and groups, and that are able to effectively address and resolve intergroup conflicts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the practice of MCOD is not a simple matter of adding diversity to the OD process.
MCOD is a powerful approach to organizational change that can be used by OD practitioners to create more inclusive, effective, and productive organizations.
OD practitioners must understand and be aware of the social context of the workplace.
